pr_body:
Currently the package.json file is only searched for within the directory and not in parent directories, this should fix this.

As discussed here: closes #167
pr_comments: @DeMoorJasper nice work! Do you think it is possible to add tests for this issue? In order to avoid future regressions?
@marcioj i'll look into it, not sure how to write tests for this though

> @marcioj i'll look into it, not sure how to write tests for this though

@DeMoorJasper I'd try to create something based on this [test](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/master/test/plugins.js#L5). You can then copy the`test/integration/plugins` and change to a subfolder like structure. Like src/index.js and src/test.txt ..
Tests should now handle parent folder package.json as well

issue_context.title: Plugins are not loaded if the entry is not on the same directory as package.json
issue_context.body:
<!---
Thanks for filing an issue 😄 ! Before you submit, please read the following:

Search open/closed issues before submitting since someone might have asked the same thing before!
-->

This is a 🐛 bug report.

<!--- Provide a general summary of the issue in the title above -->

### 🎛 Directory structure
<!--- If describing a bug, tell us what your babel configuration looks like -->

```
- package.json
+ src
  - main.js
+ node_modules
  + parcel-bundler
  + parcel-plugin-plugin
```

### 🤔 Expected Behavior
Parcel should be able to load the plugins from the `package.json`.
<!--- If you're describing a bug, tell us what should happen -->
<!--- If you're suggesting a change/improvement, tell us how it should work -->

### 😯 Current Behavior
It does not if the entry file is not in the root directory of the project.

The error is silenced but if we log it we get :
```
Error: Cannot find module './package.json' from '[project]/src'
at Function.module.exports [as sync] ([project]/node_modules/resolve/lib/sync.js:40:15)
at module.exports ([project]/node_modules/parcel-bundler/src/utils/localRequire.js:11:24)
at Bundler.loadPlugins ([project]/node_modules/parcel-bundler/src/Bundler.js:86:17)
at new Bundler ([project]/node_modules/parcel-bundler/src/Bundler.js:44:10)
at Command.bundle ([project]/node_modules/parcel-bundler/bin/cli.js:66:19)
at Command.listener ([project]/node_modules/commander/index.js:315:8)
at emitTwo (events.js:126:13)
at Command.emit (events.js:214:7)
at Command.parseArgs ([project]/node_modules/commander/index.js:653:12)
at Command.parse ([project]/node_modules/commander/index.js:475:21) code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
```

<!--- If describing a bug, tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior -->
<!--- If you are seeing an error, please include the full error message and stack trace -->
<!--- If suggesting a change/improvement, explain the difference from current behavior -->

### 💁 Possible Solution

I dirty-fixed it by replacing `./package.json` to `../package.json`, but the best solution should be to traverse the directory tree until a `package.json` is found.
<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix/reason for the bug, -->
<!--- or ideas how to implement the addition or change -->

### 🔦 Context

Found this while working on a plugin
<!--- How has this issue affected you? What are you trying to accomplish? -->
<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->

### 🌍 Your Environment
<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s)
| ---------------- | ----------
| Parcel           |  1.1.0
| Node             | 8.9.1
| npm/Yarn         | 1.3.2
| Operating System | macOS 10.13.2
comments: Path traversing up is prob a solid way to go, i'll take a look at it

There is a `pkg-up` module that currently handled this:

https://github.com/sindresorhus/pkg-up
@fathyb Are you running parcel via an npm script?
@davidnagli yes, I have `"build": "parcel src/main.js"` in my `scripts` and I run `yarn build`. Same with `$(yarn bin)/parcel src/main.js`

review_comments: Is `err` always because it isn't found, or could it be something like access denied? Wouldn't want to keep traversing if it is found but just couldn't read it. That's a legitimate error.
